subject: NA/Inf for SE while fitting Mutlilevel IRT models using mixedmirt

messages.author: df47aaa51177e924
messages.subject: NA/Inf for SE while fitting Mutlilevel IRT models using mixedmirt
parts:
Hi Phil,

Hope you are doing well.  

I got the following  warning message when I was trying to fit a mutlilevel IRT (3-level model with item responses modeled using graded response model, and within- and between-school models are at level-2 and 3) using mixedmirt.

2: In qlogis(predict(mod, data.frame(CTVs = x))) : NaNs produced 

3: In nlm(f = fn, p = CTVs[pick]) : NA/Inf replaced by maximum positive value 

4: In qlogis(predict(mod, data.frame(CTVs = x))) : NaNs produced 

5: In nlm(f = fn, p = CTVs[pick]) : NA/Inf replaced by maximum positive value

I have 16 items in the data and am fitting a GRM as the measurement model. NaN arises for the SE of the coefficient of the Public School predictor, which is an indicator variable (coded 1/0). I wonder if the NaN is due to convergence issues. Would appreciate any pointers.  

This is what my set up looked like. 

mod2 <- mixedmirt(data= hp[2:17],covdata_predictors ,model=1, +                                   fixed = ~hp.hp_rural + hp.ESCS+hp.Gender_Female+hp.PublicSchool, lr.random = ~1|hp.SchoolID, itemtype = 'graded')

The result was following 

-------------- FIXED EFFECTS: Estimate Std.Error z.value hp.

hp.PublicSchool    -0.180       NaN     NaN

I am also fitting this model in JAGS using a Bayesian approach and there I obtain very large SD's for this coefficient -- in the range of 200 and 300. I am not very sure why this might be the case -- if it is convergence issues or problems in specifying the model. 

I would appreciate any help on what could be going on.

Also, if you have the time could you tell me if the model specification seems fine for the mutlilevel IRT with level 2 and 3 as the within-school and between -school and level -1 is GRM. I am trying to wrap my head around the mixed modeling framework specification in mixed mirt. I did use lr.fixed (which I think is the correct specification as it uses the factor scores) but those results do not match and are not even close to what I obtain from JAGS. Appreciate any help.     

Thanks a lot

Jayashri

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: NA/Inf for SE while fitting Mutlilevel IRT models using mixedmirt
parts:
The lr.fixed and fixed inputs are indeed quite different, and only result in equivalent models in situations where the slope parameters are set to 1 (i.e., Rasch models). lr.fixed is the linear decomposition of the latent trait parameters, and so is generally used for latent regression models. If the model is not a Rasch one, then fixed will decompose structures of the intercepts instead. In your case, you probably want to stick with the lr.fixed inputs to "explain" difference in latent trait values given external covariantes. HTH.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: NA/Inf for SE while fitting Mutlilevel IRT models using mixedmirt
parts:
Yes, the constraint means that a Wald test wouldn't be appropriate since by definition the parameters being tested against are exactly the same with the same variability. I think you want to use a score-test instead, as this is more about what would happen if a parameter was allowed to differ. You could also just do a likelihood-ratio test between the two models as you would have nested variants of each other, and for the most part the LR test is better than either the score or Wald when it is possible to fit both models. HTH.

Phil
